note_sections.t: Re-evaluation is requested following a sustained PSA rise to 8.0 ng/mL and a recent multiparametric MRI demonstrating a high-suspicion transition zone lesion.

Long-standing referral for urological assessment highlights a 74-year-old mechanical engineer who recently navigated a period of elevated prostate-specific antigen levels preceding his initial tissue sampling. He manages moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS of 9, currently treated with daily tamsulosin, and maintains a sedentary-friendly routine supplemented by light home weight training twice weekly. His past medical history is otherwise notable only for benign prostatic hyperplasia, and he remains a lifelong non-smoker who abstains from alcohol. Socially, he resides with his partner, who serves as his primary contact, and he recently completed a routine biannual dental examination without complications. He acknowledges considerable anxiety surrounding invasive procedures and has requested additional consultation time to discuss diagnostic findings thoroughly.

Per rectum, the prostate gland feels smooth and symmetrically enlarged without discrete nodularity or induration, correlating with a clinical stage of cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished individual with stable vital signs and clear respiratory fields. Abdominal inspection is unremarkable, and there is no palpable lymphadenopathy or organomegaly.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
